## 固定收益開篇論述

6月8日，美債延續上週五非農就業數據引發的賣壓。以色列與伊朗再度交戰推高油價，投資人持續評估就業韌性與新一輪能源衝擊是否會迫使聯準會升息。跌勢不再集中於政策敏感的短端：2年期殖利率上升1.6個基點至4.164%，5年期上升2.2個基點至4.291%，10年期上升3.3個基點至4.564%，30年期則上升4個基點至5.037%。

這與上週五由短端急遽領跌的重新定價不同。長端表現落後，使2年與10年期利差擴大1.7個基點至40個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大2.4個基點至87.3個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升3.7個基點至2.199%，損益兩平通膨率反而下降0.4個基點至2.365%。即使WTI上漲0.84%至$91.30、布蘭特原油上漲1.25%至$94.25，投資人提高的仍是持有各天期債券所要求的通膨調整後報酬，並未同步增加對長期通膨的補償要求。

紐約聯準銀行的家庭調查提供了重要的反向訊號，但不足以扭轉收盤走勢。1年期通膨預期由3.6%降至3.5%，3年與5年期預期則分別維持3.1%及3.0%。與此同時，受訪者對就業及家庭財務更為擔憂：自認失業的機率上升、失業後另覓工作的機率下降，無法支付最低債務還款額的機率也提高。調查結果削弱了通膨心理持續惡化的論點，卻無法取代強勁非農報告在政策展望中的分量，也未消除眼前的油價風險。

跨資產市場的收盤表現比債市正面。標普500指數上漲0.30%，那斯達克100指數上漲1.58%，費城半導體指數反彈5.61%，VIX則下跌12.04%至18.92；高收益債基金也小幅走高。這並非全面避險：股市自上週五由科技股帶動的跌勢中反彈之際，美債市場重新評估的是持有利率部位所需的實質利率及供給補償。

全球數據仍加深成長疲弱與抑制通膨之間的矛盾。德國4月製造業訂單降幅遠超預期；經濟學家警告，若ECB在經濟活動收縮之際對能源衝擊反應過度，這次可能的升息恐重蹈以往錯誤。韓國面對的問題正好相反：半導體投資、較強勁的成長、核心通膨及潛在財政供給，共同引發政府債券重挫。能源是這些市場共同面對的擾動因素，但各地內需與政策環境決定了能源衝擊究竟會強化緊縮壓力，還是凸顯緊縮的代價。

## 實質殖利率領跌，美債跌勢擴大

美債市場週一開盤時仍在消化上週五意外強勁的就業數據。亞洲交易時段殖利率一度普遍上升約2至5個基點，以2年與5年期領跌；交易員重新反映聯準會在12月前升息25個基點的可能性，並賦予第二次升息約16%的機率。就在幾天前，市場仍要到2027年3月才完全反映首次升息。5月非農就業成長高於所有預測，前幾個月數據又獲上修，使市場更難指望勞動市場轉弱能阻止政策進一步緊縮。

油價構成第二股壓力。伊朗發動飛彈攻擊後，以色列再度空襲伊朗，持久停火的希望因而受挫。布蘭特原油在市場全面反應期間一度升破$97，最終收於$94.25，當日仍上漲。能源成本因此仍可能推升近期通膨，使聯準會更難維持偏向寬鬆的政策立場。

美債最終跌勢比亞洲時段初期更為分散。30年期殖利率上升4個基點，在主要天期中漲幅最大，重新站上5%；2年期升幅則不到2個基點。這種熊市陡峭化顯示，市場調整的不再只是下一次政策行動的時點。在通膨路徑不確定、公私部門融資需求龐大、地緣政治風險溢價尚未穩定的環境下，投資人也要求更高的實質補償，才願意持有較長天期債券。

10年期殖利率的拆解更清楚呈現這項差異。名目殖利率上升3.3個基點，略低於實質殖利率的3.7個基點升幅，損益兩平通膨率則下降。以一週來看，10年期實質殖利率上升15.6個基點，名目殖利率上升11個基點，通膨補償下降4.6個基點；以一個月來看，實質殖利率上升30.5個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降9.6個基點。市場持續提高持有利率部位所要求的通膨調整後利率，而非把能源衝擊外推為不斷升高的長期通膨預期。

美國總統Donald Trump在週日播出的訪談中反對這種重新定價。他表示聯準會沒有升息理由，借貸成本反而應該降低。不過，這番言論並未改變市場的基本判斷：強勁就業讓央行有空間因應高於目標的通膨。Kevin Warsh就任主席後的首次FOMC會議將於6月16日至17日舉行；屆時市場定價正朝緊縮移動，任命他的總統卻公開主張寬鬆。

紐約聯準銀行消費者預期調查則從另一方向增加鷹派論點的複雜度。1年期通膨預期中位數下降0.1個百分點至3.5%，3年與5年期讀數均未改變，沒有證據顯示最新能源衝擊已推高家庭的長期通膨預期。這項差異相當重要：比起燃料價格一次性上升，持續惡化的通膨心理才會使再次升息更具急迫性。

同一調查的其他結果顯示家庭脆弱性上升。受訪者認為未來一年失業的機率增加0.5個百分點至15.1%；在預期自己將失業的人當中，自認能找到另一份工作的機率下降2.3個百分點至43.7%。無法支付最低債務還款額的機率上升1.2個百分點至12.6%，預期家庭支出成長率則下降0.4個百分點至5%。

這些惡化訊號並未推翻官方就業報告，卻顯示已實現的非農就業成長強勁之際，家庭對工作保障、重新就業及償債能力的信心正在轉弱。聯準會因此必須區分目前勞動需求的水準，以及家庭預期情勢將朝哪個方向發展。若官員認為非農就業的強勢將會消退，這份調查支持保持耐心；若後續通膨壓力擴大且就業依然穩健，調查對升息形成的阻力就較小。

美債現貨交易量低於上週五異常熱絡的水準。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$9,668億、共324,026筆，較前一交易日下降17.6%；名目附息債交易量下降23.9%至$7,607億。剩餘年期2年以下的附息債交易量減少35.2%，超過3年至5年期的區段減少18.3%，超過7年至10年期的區段則減少26.3%。交易量下降顯示，非農衝擊後的賣勢是在較低成交活動下延續，但無法據此判斷客戶交易方向。

國庫券標售順利消化，需求訊號卻不一致。財政部標售$890.01億13週期國庫券，最高得標利率為3.640%，高於前次的3.630%。投標倍數由2.69改善至2.79；間接投標人取得獲接受競爭性投標的56.22%，直接投標人取得5.87%，交易商承接37.90%。該券於6月11日發行並交割，9月10日到期。

$770億的26週期國庫券標售最高得標利率為3.690%，高於前次的3.665%。投標倍數由2.84降至2.75，間接投標人占53.91%，直接投標人占5.53%，交易商承接40.56%。該券同樣於6月11日交割，12月10日到期。兩場標售的獲接受金額均未改變，得標利率則雙雙上升；13週期投標倍數改善，與26週期需求轉弱、交易商承接比例增加形成對比。

## 歐洲成長證據考驗ECB的抗通膨回應

德國4月製造業訂單下降3.8%，降幅超過預期1.2%的三倍，並回吐3月經修正後4.5%增幅的一部分。疲弱程度已足以影響ECB決策中的成長考量，而地區分布更顯示歐元區內部需求出現格外嚴重的萎縮。

外國訂單月減4.2%，其中來自歐元區的訂單驟減11.1%；歐元區以外訂單增加0.8%，國內需求則下降2.9%。訂單較一年前仍高出1.6%，但2月至4月合計比之前三個月低3.1%。這顯示工業景氣承接力道疲弱，並非單月總體數字的簡單修正。

數據公布三天後，ECB將舉行政策會議，目前市場普遍預期將存款利率調升25個基點至2.25%。支持升息的理由包括歐元區通膨達到3.2%、基礎價格壓力增強、企業漲價意向仍高，以及家庭可能把能源衝擊納入通膨預期的疑慮。包括執行理事Isabel Schnabel與希臘央行總裁Yannis Stournaras在內，政策立場各異的官員都已表示，不能再一概忽略這次衝擊。

爭議在於，升息究竟能遏制第二輪效應，還是會對已失去動能的經濟施加不必要的限制。愛爾蘭數據大幅修正後，歐元區產出在年初出現收縮；若排除愛爾蘭，推算成長率則約為0.2%至0.3%。商業活動正以2024年以來最快速度萎縮，法國尤其疲弱。德國訂單報告進一步提供實質證據，顯示在能源成本上升的完整衝擊或另一次升息到來前，工業需求已相當脆弱。

反對立即採取行動的經濟學家援引ECB在2008年及2011年的政策逆轉：當時為捍衛通膨公信力而升息，卻在金融及經濟情勢惡化後迅速轉向寬鬆。這段歷史本身並不代表相同結果必然重演，但點出了當前風險：即使能源衝擊消退、經濟活動繼續收縮，市場仍可能把一次防範性升息解讀為一連串升息的起點。

前ECB首席經濟學家Peter Praet認為，決策官員終究必須展現採取行動的意願，但強調不應把一次升息表述為連續數次行動的開端。現任職Morgan Stanley的前ECB經濟學家Jens Eisenschmidt預期未來幾個月將升息兩次，且兩次升息都會在明年逆轉；他認為這種先升後降是因應情勢變化的調整，不能證明原本的升息決定有誤。PGIM的Katharine Neiss則預期，若調查與經濟活動明顯惡化，官員會保留降息空間。

另一派意見認為，目前尚無第二輪薪資壓力的確切證據。Societe Generale的Michala Marcussen警告，在這類證據出現前緊縮，可能造成沒有必要的額外限制。Berenberg的Holger Schmieding則主張，疲弱需求無論如何都可能消散通膨壓力，升息只會讓家庭與企業承擔額外政策成本。

因此，會後溝通至少與市場預期的首次行動同樣重要。投資人與經濟學家普遍預期2026年升息不只一次，但成長數據使持續緊縮的訊號更難成立。若升息同時強調後續行動取決於條件，便可區分防止通膨預期失去錨定的措施與新的固定升息循環。反之，若指引認可反覆升息，即使訂單與商業活動惡化，歐洲短端利率仍將承受更大上行壓力。

英國另有一項財政發展。據報政府計畫未來四年削減£60億投資，受影響項目包括學校及醫院，以協助籌措增加£150億國防支出所需資金。這項調整改變的是公共支出組成，而非單純改變總額：民用投資減少，更多資源轉向國防。目前沒有相應的債市觀察，無法據此確認英國公債當日受到何種影響，但這項安排顯示安全壓力正在促使各國政府更廣泛地重新分配預算。

## 韓國景氣擴張與日本需求將亞洲債券推向相反方向

南韓政府債券已成為區內最明顯的案例，顯示國內成長如何放大全球能源與通膨衝擊。2026年以當地貨幣計價，南韓債市已下跌7.5%，在所引述比較的44個市場中表現最差；基準3年期殖利率上週五升至約3.9%，為2023年以來最高。另據週一市場報導，在區內科技股遭到拋售之際，10年期殖利率飆升36個基點，創一年多來最高水準。

壓力來源並不限於避險情緒。AI投資與半導體需求帶動成長復甦、資本支出增加，並改善晶片出口展望。韓國央行把2026年成長預測由2%上調至2.6%；5月核心通膨達2.5%，顯示價格壓力正由能源向外擴散。高房價與韓元疲弱也分別增加國內及輸入性通膨風險。

交換市場已反映韓國央行年內至少升息三次，政策利率將由2.5%升至3.25%。Shinyoung Securities策略師Cho Yong-gu預期，3年與10年期殖利率最高可能分別達到4%及4.4%。KB Securities的Lim Jae-kyun估計，若政策利率升至3.5%，10年期殖利率可能達4.4%。這些看法顯示，債市賣壓來自較強勁的名目成長與央行立場轉鷹，而不只是美債走勢外溢。

財政政策是另一項不確定因素。官員3月曾表示，為追加預算融資不需要增發債券；但市場持續討論另一套方案及即將到來的2027年度預算，使交易員警戒供給可能增加。政府為抑制波動，把6月原定公債發行量較5月削減約21%，主要減少較長天期債券。財政部債券官員也直接聯絡交易商及資產管理業者，並與市場參與者和研究人員成立私人聊天群組，以監控市場情況。

這些措施可降低近期供給並改善溝通，卻無法消除殖利率上升的根本力量。半導體熱潮已在推升經濟活動，韓元疲弱又增加進口成本，此時若推出大規模財政方案，將進一步支撐需求。韓國央行在總裁Shin Hyun Song領導下轉向鷹派；若核心通膨保持強勁，市場仍可能進一步重新定價。

日本機構投資人的需求則為全球債券提供反向資金流。通常被視為退休基金代理指標的銀行信託帳戶，5月淨買入¥3.16兆海外債券，為2005年有數據以來最高。SMBC Nikko策略師Miki Den表示，其中很大一部分可能流向美國；美國10年期公債殖利率5月19日曾升至4.69%，為2025年1月以來最高。

這筆創紀錄買盤反映的是5月已發生的資金流，不能證明日本投資人買進了週一遭拋售的美債。不過，即使日本政府債券殖利率也在上升，數據仍顯示較高的美債殖利率能吸引大規模策略性需求。日本可比殖利率在自身5月中旬高點時仍比美國基準低約200個基點，因此在計入匯率避險及其他成本前，兩者仍有可觀的殖利率差距。

Miki Den預期，由於中東局勢及聯準會政策的不確定性仍高，近期購買速度可能放慢，待兩者走向更明朗後才恢復。這項但書對即將到來的美債標售週期十分重要。5月創紀錄的需求證明投資人具備承接能力與意願，但地緣政治波動及聯準會可能緊縮，會使資金延後進場，而此時財政部正要求投資人吸收新的附息債供給。

## 亞洲信用市場區分再融資能力與國家支持

印尼市場重挫正開始與新的美元融資直接交會。主權財富基金Danantara計畫6月9日在波士頓啟動債券路演的美國行程，隔日再前往紐約。該基金官員先前在亞洲舉行會議時曾告訴部分投資人，潛在募資所得的一部分可用於再融資2026年稍早取得的一筆$10億貸款。

這次發債之際，印尼盾已跌至歷史低點，投資人擔心總統Prabowo Subianto的干預式經濟政策，印尼股市因而延續跌勢。基準股價指數週一下跌逾4%，2026年累計跌幅接近40%。印尼10年期政府公債殖利率升至一年多來最高，財政與央行官員因此面臨更大壓力，必須在週末安撫市場之外，提出能吸引資金流入的具體措施。

相較之下，美元主權債仍有韌性。截至上週五，一籃子印尼政府債券的利差在2026年僅擴大約3個基點至71個基點；同期亞洲高評級美元債利差收窄13個基點，降至歷史低點50個基點。這項對比顯示，印尼雖落後於強勁的區域信用市場，美元債卻尚未出現印尼盾、當地利率或股市那般失序的情況。

Danantara與政府的法律關係將是路演核心。發行備忘錄指出，政府不為本次債券的償付義務提供保證；募資所得可用於一般公司用途，包括投資及再融資未償借款。這項區別至關重要：Danantara統轄近900家國營企業，也是政府經濟政策的重要工具，但其制度角色不會使擬議債券自動成為具有明確政府保證的主權債務。

該基金也計畫向境內外投資人發行以當地貨幣計價、票息3%的「Merah Putih」債券，票息低於當前市場利率。在決策官員力圖穩定匯率、恢復信心之際，Danantara同時尋求美元資金與受補貼的當地貨幣融資，投資人因而會更加重視可取得的條件及確切償債來源。

菲律賓面臨的企業再融資考驗較慢浮現，但規模可觀。一份跨機關金融穩定報告指出，大型企業集團在2027年至2029年間約有1.6兆披索、即$260億債務到期，接近這些集團總債務的四分之一；未來五年，美元債務平均占其債務的37.6%。

企業迄今透過發債、銀行融資及內部流動性滿足再融資需求。不過，披索疲弱增加外幣債務換算為當地貨幣後的負擔，而菲律賓幾乎所有燃料都從中東進口。即使眼前沒有違約事件，匯率貶值、能源成本上升與到期債務集中，仍同時提高再融資及外匯風險。

報告表示，銀行資本仍足以吸收意外損失，且能繼續放款；但房地產價格偏高及無擔保消費借款增加亦構成脆弱環節，後者主要為信用卡債務。菲律賓央行總裁Eli Remolona表示，監管機關將界定問題應在何時升級處理，並改善有關受監管實體的溝通。因此，新資訊是在監管機關仍稱穩定的金融體系中，具體量化其到期債務及外幣曝險。

其他市場的初級發行活動顯示，投資人仍願意為大型交易提供資金。Tencent正籌備約$30億的雙幣債券發行，最快可於週二定價。Blackstone尋求把逾$20億的私募基金持份轉化為債券，可能成為近年同類型交易中規模最大的案例之一。Arcmont Asset Management與Ares則主導一筆€11億貸款，借款人為Silver Lake支持的法國軟體公司Cegid。這些交易顯示結構型及槓桿融資管道仍然暢通，但投資人承擔的基礎現金流風險與傳統優先順位公司債不同。

更廣泛的總體風險仍取決於油價衝擊持續多久。Peterson Institute for International Economics的一項情境分析假設油價在整整一年內維持每桶約$120，液化天然氣、成品油、農產品及肥料也同步漲價。相較基準情境，模型估計中東與北非產出將至少降低12%，印度、越南及泰國約降低3%，南韓降低2.8%，中國降低1.8%，西歐降低1.6%，美國降低1.2%。

這些是附帶條件的模型估計，並非預測；週一油價收在$90至$95區間。不過，分析仍說明同一項衝擊為何會產生不同的信用結果。能源進口國面臨成長轉弱、匯率壓力及再融資成本上升；內需較強的經濟體則可能以更緊縮的貨幣政策回應。在該情境中，美國受到的整體影響相對有限，但農業與運輸業所受衝擊仍會大於整體經濟。

## 前瞻市場意義

下一輪美債需求考驗將於6月9日開始。財政部在美東時間11:30標售$650億6週期國庫券及$500億52週期國庫券；6週期發行額比前次少$100億，52週期規模不變。美東時間13:00將標售$580億新發3年期公債，規模與前次相同，於6月15日交割。在非農公布後連續兩個交易日下跌之後，這場標售將顯示較高殖利率能否吸引資金承接政策敏感的殖利率曲線中段債券。

6月10日美東時間08:30公布的美國CPI是最關鍵的總體事件。整體通膨預期月增0.5%、年增4.2%，前值分別為0.6%及3.8%；核心通膨預期月增0.2%、年增2.9%，前值分別為0.4%及2.8%。若升幅主要來自能源，將與10年期損益兩平通膨率下降一致；若核心價格普遍強勁，則會支持實質殖利率上升，並強化聯準會最終升息的理由。

CPI公布後，財政部將於美東時間13:00增額發行$390億10年期公債，票息為4.375%，6月15日交割。本週最重要的通膨數據公布後隨即標售較長天期債券；在10年期實質殖利率升至2.199%後，得標水準及投標人組成均將具有重要意義。

ECB將於6月11日美東時間08:15公布政策決定。升息25個基點會使存款利率由2%升至2.25%，但更重要的是管理委員會會將此舉定位為有限的防範措施，還是連續緊縮的開端。德國6月9日公布4月工業生產，市場預期在前值修正為下降0.1%後回升0.5%；數據將顯示訂單重挫是否已傳導至實際產出。

美國6月11日美東時間08:30公布生產者物價與初領失業救濟金人數。PPI預期月增0.7%，核心指標預期上升0.5%，前值經修正後分別增加1.4%及1%。初領失業救濟金人數的前值為225,000人，這次數據將檢驗家庭對失業的憂慮是否開始反映在實際裁員上。財政部隨後於美東時間13:00增額發行$220億30年期公債，完成本輪附息債標售。

三筆附息債均於6月15日交割，總交割額達$1,190億，時間就在6月16日至17日FOMC會議之前。30年期殖利率重新升破5%後，如此集中的交割將考驗交易商資產負債表及最終投資人的需求。6月15日也將公布美國工業生產，市場預期在前值成長0.9%後增加0.1%，為聯準會決策前最後一項實質經濟活動更新。

亞洲較近期的行事曆由中國5月貿易數據揭開序幕，公布時間為6月9日台北時間10:30。貿易順差預期由CNY5,856億增至CNY6,250億；進出口細項將顯示外部需求能否繼續支撐區域製造業。印尼方面，Danantara在波士頓及紐約舉行的會議將測試投資人是否願意承擔國營基金缺乏明確政府保證的公司型風險。韓國方面，眼前要觀察的是：在成長轉強、核心通膨偏高及市場預期韓國央行至少升息三次的情況下，削減6月債券發行量能否遏止跌勢。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。利率資料採用Bloomberg每日殖利率歷史序列；變動幅度及衍生殖利率曲線均以相同日期序列計算。每日歷史資料未指定觀察時間。

overall_summary.headline: 非農就業強勁、油價風險再起，實質殖利率與長端承壓，美債跌勢擴大
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美債延續上週五非農就業數據引發的跌勢，但賣壓由政策敏感的短端擴大為熊市陡峭化。2年期殖利率上升1.6個基點至4.164%，10年期上升3.3個基點至4.564%，30年期上升4個基點至5.037%。10年期實質殖利率上升3.7個基點至2.199%，損益兩平通膨率則下降0.4個基點至2.365%，顯示投資人要求更高的通膨調整後補償，而非把能源衝擊外推為更高的長期通膨預期。

5月非農就業優於預期，加上以色列與伊朗再度交戰，使市場持續承壓；WTI上漲0.84%至$91.30，布蘭特原油上漲1.25%至$94.25。紐約聯準銀行調查稍微緩和鷹派論點：1年期通膨預期降至3.5%，較長期讀數持平，家庭也更加擔心失業、重新就業及債務還款。這些訊號仍不足以取代已實現就業數據的韌性，也未消除眼前的油價風險。

跨資產市場收盤較為正面。股市反彈，半導體股領漲，波動率下降，高收益債基金也小幅走高，顯示市場並未全面轉向避險。下一項考驗是CPI與美債附息債標售週期能否支持實質殖利率上升，同時在較高名目利率下吸引足夠需求。
overall_summary.summary: 強勁就業與以色列、伊朗再度交戰延續緊縮及通膨疑慮，美債殖利率全線上升、長端表現落後；家庭通膨預期下降及信心轉弱僅形成部分制衡。

section_summaries.market_read: 長端表現落後，顯示重新定價已不只針對聯準會下一次行動的時點，也擴及投資人持有較長天期債券所要求的補償。
section_summaries.summary: 市場消化強勁非農就業、油價風險再起及長端融資負擔，美債呈現熊市陡峭化。10年期走勢由實質殖利率上升主導，而非長期通膨補償提高。家庭通膨預期下降，對就業與償債能力的擔憂則加深，使緊縮理由更為複雜但未遭逆轉；股市走強也顯示債市賣壓並非全面避險。

section_summaries.market_read: 實質殖利率在單日、一週及一個月均上升，顯示投資人要求更高的實質補償，而非反映持續性通膨。
section_summaries.section_title: 實質殖利率領跌，美債跌勢擴大
section_summaries.summary: 非農公布後的美債跌勢延續，市場重新反映聯準會在12月前升息，以色列與伊朗再度交戰則使能源通膨風險受到關注。30年期殖利率重返5%以上；10年期實質殖利率升幅超過名目殖利率，損益兩平通膨率反而下降。家庭通膨預期仍保持穩定，但對工作保障及償債能力的信心轉弱，使官員必須在已實現就業強勁與脆弱性訊號之間權衡。

section_summaries.market_read: 以條件為基礎的政策指引可抑制通膨預期，又不必承諾展開疲弱需求可能無法承受的升息循環。
section_summaries.section_title: 歐洲成長證據考驗ECB的抗通膨回應
section_summaries.summary: 德國4月製造業訂單下降3.8%，其中歐元區訂單驟減11.1%，在市場預期ECB升息前，進一步提供工業需求疲弱的實質證據。核心問題是官員會把存款利率升至2.25%定位為防範第二輪通膨的有限措施，還是在經濟活動收縮之際展開連續緊縮。英國另計畫把支出由民用投資轉向國防。

section_summaries.market_read: 韓國的重新定價反映國內名目成長轉強與央行立場轉鷹，而不只是美債走勢外溢。
section_summaries.next_check: 在核心通膨與進一步升息預期仍強的情況下，削減6月債券發行量能否遏止韓國債市跌勢。
section_summaries.section_title: 韓國景氣擴張與日本需求將亞洲債券推向相反方向
section_summaries.summary: 半導體帶動成長、核心通膨達2.5%、韓元疲弱及潛在財政供給，共同強化市場對韓國央行至少升息三次的預期，南韓債券因而遭到拋售。削減6月發行量或可緩和近期壓力，卻未消除上述因素。日本銀行信託帳戶5月創紀錄買進海外債券，提供反向需求訊號，但地緣政治及聯準會政策的不確定性可能延後後續買盤。

section_summaries.market_read: 與政府的制度關係不能取代明確保證；償債來源及發行條件仍是評估Danantara信用風險的核心。
section_summaries.section_title: 亞洲信用市場區分再融資能力與國家支持
section_summaries.summary: 印尼盾、當地債券及股市仍承壓之際，Danantara的美元債路演將測試投資人對這家重要印尼國營基金債務的需求，其債券並無明確政府保證。菲律賓企業集團在2027年至2029年間面臨1.6兆披索債務到期，美元曝險也相當可觀，但監管機關表示銀行資本仍然充足。其他大型融資交易則顯示初級市場管道保持暢通。
美國CPI及隨後的10年期公債增額發行，將檢驗核心通膨是否普遍強勁、足以支持實質殖利率上升，以及投資人是否願意在新的殖利率水準承接較長天期債券。德國經濟活動轉弱之際，ECB必須區分有限的抗通膨保險措施與持續升息循環。整輪附息債標售將在6月16日至17日FOMC會議前形成$1,190億交割額，考驗交易商承接能力及最終投資人需求。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended Friday’s payroll-driven selloff on June 8 as renewed fighting between Israel and Iran lifted oil and kept investors focused on the risk that resilient employment and another energy shock will force the Federal Reserve to raise rates. The move broadened beyond the policy-sensitive front end: the 2-year yield rose 1.6 basis points to 4.164%, the 5-year increased 2.2 basis points to 4.291%, the 10-year added 3.3 basis points to 4.564% and the 30-year climbed 4 basis points to 5.037%.

That pattern differed from Friday’s sharp front-end-led repricing. The 2s10s curve steepened 1.7 basis points to 40 basis points and 2s30s widened 2.4 basis points to 87.3 basis points as the long end underperformed. At 10 years, the real yield rose 3.7 basis points to 2.199%, while breakeven inflation slipped 0.4 basis point to 2.365%. Investors therefore demanded a higher inflation-adjusted return across the curve without adding to long-horizon inflation compensation, even as WTI gained 0.84% to $91.30 and Brent rose 1.25% to $94.25.

A New York Fed household survey supplied a meaningful counterweight but not enough to reverse the close. One-year inflation expectations declined to 3.5% from 3.6%, and expectations at three and five years held at 3.1% and 3.0%. At the same time, respondents became more worried about employment and household finances: the perceived probability of losing a job rose, the chance of finding another job fell and the probability of missing a minimum debt payment increased. Those results weakened the case that inflation psychology was deteriorating, but they did not displace the stronger payroll report or remove the immediate oil risk from the policy outlook.

The cross-asset close was more constructive than the bond market. The S&P 500 rose 0.30%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.58% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index rebounded 5.61%, while the VIX fell 12.04% to 18.92. High-yield funds also edged higher. The combination was not a general flight from risk: Treasuries were repricing the real rate and supply required to hold duration as equities recovered from Friday’s technology-led decline.

Global evidence nevertheless added to the tension between weak growth and inflation restraint. German manufacturing orders fell much more than expected in April, while economists warned that a likely ECB increase could repeat earlier mistakes if officials react too aggressively to an energy shock as activity contracts. Korea presented the opposite problem, with semiconductor investment, stronger growth, core inflation and potential fiscal supply driving a severe government-bond selloff. Across those markets, energy remained the common disturbance, but domestic demand and policy conditions determined whether it reinforced tightening or exposed the cost of it.

## Real Yields Lead a Broader Treasury Decline

The Treasury market entered Monday still absorbing Friday’s employment surprise. Asian trading initially pushed yields roughly 2 to 5 basis points higher, led by 2- and 5-year notes, as traders returned to pricing a quarter-point Fed increase by December and assigned about a 16% probability to a second move. Only days earlier, the first full increase had not been priced until March 2027. The May payroll result, which exceeded every forecast and included upward revisions to prior months, made it harder to rely on labor weakness as protection against tighter policy.

Oil added a second source of pressure after fresh Israeli strikes on Iran followed a missile attack and imperiled hopes for a durable ceasefire. Brent traded above $97 during the broader market response before ending at $94.25. The close still left crude higher on the day, preserving the possibility that energy costs will lift near-term inflation and make it more difficult for the Fed to maintain an easing bias.

The completed Treasury move was less concentrated than the initial Asian selloff. The 30-year yield’s 4-basis-point increase was the largest among the main tenors, taking it back above 5%, while the 2-year rose by less than 2 basis points. That bear-steepening configuration suggests the market was no longer adjusting only the date of the next policy move. Investors also required additional real compensation to hold longer-duration bonds in an environment combining an uncertain inflation path, substantial public and private financing needs and an unsettled geopolitical risk premium.

The 10-year decomposition sharpens that distinction. Its nominal yield increased 3.3 basis points, slightly less than the 3.7-basis-point rise in the real yield, while the breakeven declined. Over one week, the 10-year real yield had risen 15.6 basis points, compared with an 11-basis-point increase in the nominal yield and a 4.6-basis-point decline in inflation compensation. Over one month, the real yield was up 30.5 basis points and the breakeven down 9.6 basis points. The market has consistently raised the inflation-adjusted rate required on duration rather than extrapolating the energy shock into ever-higher long-term inflation expectations.

President Donald Trump opposed that repricing in an interview aired Sunday. He said there was no reason for the Fed to raise rates and argued that borrowing costs should instead be lowered. The comments did not alter the basic market judgment that strong employment gives the central bank room to respond to above-target inflation. Chairman Kevin Warsh’s first FOMC meeting on June 16-17 will therefore begin with market pricing moving toward tightening while the president who appointed him publicly argues for easing.

The New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations complicated the hawkish case from a different direction. Median one-year inflation expectations fell 0.1 percentage point to 3.5%, while the unchanged three- and five-year readings offered no evidence that the latest energy shock had pushed longer-term household expectations higher. That matters because persistent inflation psychology, rather than a one-time increase in fuel prices, would make the case for another increase more urgent.

Households reported greater vulnerability elsewhere in the survey. The perceived probability of losing a job over the next year rose 0.5 percentage point to 15.1%. Among those expecting to lose employment, the perceived chance of finding another job declined 2.3 percentage points to 43.7%. The probability of missing a minimum debt payment increased 1.2 percentage points to 12.6%, while expected household spending growth fell 0.4 percentage point to 5%.

The deterioration does not undo the official employment report. It does show that strong realized payroll growth coexists with weaker household confidence in job security, re-employment and debt service. The Fed must therefore distinguish between the current level of labor demand and the direction households expect conditions to take. The survey supports patience if officials believe the payroll strength will fade; it offers less resistance to a hike if incoming inflation data broaden while employment remains firm.

Treasury cash activity declined from Friday’s unusually heavy turnover. FINRA recorded $966.8 billion of par activity across 324,026 trades, down 17.6% from the previous session. Nominal-coupon activity fell 23.9% to $760.7 billion. Turnover declined 35.2% in coupons with 2 years or less remaining, 18.3% in the sector above 3 and through 5 years, and 26.3% in securities above 7 and through 10 years. The lower volume shows the selloff extended on less activity after the payroll shock; it does not identify the direction of customer trades.

Bill auctions were absorbed without a uniform demand signal. Treasury’s $89.001 billion 13-week sale stopped at a 3.640% high rate, up from 3.630% previously. Bid-to-cover improved to 2.79 from 2.69, and indirect bidders took 56.22% of accepted competitive tenders. Direct bidders received 5.87%, leaving dealers with 37.90%. The bill is issued and settles June 11 and matures September 10.

The $77 billion 26-week auction stopped at 3.690%, compared with 3.665% at the prior sale. Its bid-to-cover ratio weakened to 2.75 from 2.84, indirect participation was 53.91%, direct bidders took 5.53% and dealers received 40.56%. It also settles June 11 and matures December 10. Both auctions cleared at higher rates on unchanged accepted amounts, but the improvement in 13-week cover contrasted with softer demand and a larger dealer share at 26 weeks.

## Europe’s Growth Evidence Tests the ECB’s Inflation Response

German manufacturing orders fell 3.8% in April, more than three times the 1.2% decline expected and reversing part of a revised 4.5% March increase. The weakness was broad enough to matter for the growth side of the ECB’s decision, although its geographic composition showed a particularly severe contraction in demand from the euro area.

Foreign orders dropped 4.2% on the month as euro-area bookings plunged 11.1%. Orders from outside the currency bloc increased 0.8%, while domestic demand fell 2.9%. Compared with a year earlier, orders were still 1.6% higher, but the February-through-April period was 3.1% below the preceding three months. The result points to a weak industrial handoff rather than a simple correction in one monthly headline.

That evidence arrived three days before an ECB meeting at which a 25-basis-point increase in the deposit rate to 2.25% forms the prevailing expectation. The case for action rests on euro-area inflation reaching 3.2%, stronger underlying pressure, elevated company pricing plans and concern that households could incorporate the energy shock into expectations. Officials across the policy spectrum, including Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel and Greek central-bank chief Yannis Stournaras, have indicated that the shock can no longer automatically be looked through.

The dispute is over whether an increase would contain second-round effects or impose unnecessary restraint on an economy already losing momentum. Euro-area output contracted at the start of the year after a large Irish revision, although calculations excluding Ireland showed growth of about 0.2% to 0.3%. Business activity has been shrinking at its quickest pace since 2024, with particular weakness in France. Germany’s order report adds hard evidence that industrial demand is vulnerable before the full impact of higher energy costs or another rate move.

Economists warning against immediate action have invoked the ECB’s 2008 and 2011 reversals, when rate increases intended to protect inflation credibility preceded abrupt easing as financial and economic conditions deteriorated. The historical parallel is not itself evidence that the same outcome will recur. It identifies the present risk: markets could interpret an insurance increase as the beginning of a series even if the energy shock fades and activity continues to contract.

Former ECB Chief Economist Peter Praet argued that policymakers eventually need to demonstrate a willingness to act, but stressed that an increase should not be presented as the first of several. Former ECB economist Jens Eisenschmidt of Morgan Stanley expects two increases in coming months and both to be reversed next year, treating that sequence as an adjustment to changing conditions rather than proof that the original moves were errors. PGIM’s Katharine Neiss expects officials to preserve room to cut if surveys and activity deteriorate materially.

The alternative view is that there is not yet firm evidence of second-round wage pressure. Societe Generale’s Michala Marcussen warned that tightening before such evidence appears would risk an unwarranted increase in restraint. Berenberg’s Holger Schmieding argued that weak demand is likely to dissipate inflation pressure regardless, leaving households and companies to bear an additional policy cost.

The meeting’s communication therefore matters at least as much as the expected first move. Investors and economists have been pricing more than one increase during 2026, but the growth data make a serial tightening signal harder to sustain. A rate rise accompanied by emphasis on conditionality would distinguish protection against de-anchoring from a new fixed hiking cycle. Guidance that validates repeated increases would put greater pressure on front-end European rates despite the deterioration in orders and business activity.

The United Kingdom supplied a separate fiscal development. The government was reported to be planning £6 billion of investment cuts over four years, affecting projects including schools and hospitals, to help finance a £15 billion increase in defense spending. The shift changes the composition rather than simply the total of public expenditure, reducing civilian investment while directing more resources toward defense. Without corresponding bond-market observations, it does not establish a same-day gilt effect, but it adds to the broader reallocation of government budgets prompted by security pressures.

## Korea’s Boom and Japanese Demand Pull Asian Duration in Opposite Directions

South Korean government bonds have become the clearest regional example of domestic growth amplifying the global energy and inflation shock. The market had lost 7.5% in local-currency terms in 2026, the worst performance among 44 markets in the cited comparison, while the benchmark 3-year yield reached about 3.9% on Friday, its highest since 2023. On Monday, separate market reporting showed the 10-year yield surging 36 basis points to its highest in more than a year as regional technology shares sold off.

The underlying pressure extends beyond risk aversion. AI investment and semiconductor demand have revived growth, increased capital spending and strengthened the outlook for chip exports. The Bank of Korea raised its 2026 growth forecast to 2.6% from 2%. Core inflation reached 2.5% in May, suggesting that price pressure was spreading beyond energy, while high apartment prices and a weak won added domestic and imported inflation risk.

Swaps were pricing at least three Bank of Korea increases during the year, which would take the policy rate to 3.25% from 2.5%. Shinyoung Securities strategist Cho Yong-gu expected 3- and 10-year yields to reach as high as 4% and 4.4%, respectively. KB Securities’ Lim Jae-kyun estimated that the 10-year could reach 4.4% if the policy rate rose to 3.5%. Those views locate the selloff in a combination of stronger nominal growth and a more hawkish central bank, not merely contagion from U.S. Treasuries.

Fiscal policy is another source of uncertainty. Officials said in March that no additional bond issuance would be needed to finance a supplementary budget, but discussion of another package and the coming 2027 budget has kept traders alert to larger supply. The government sought to contain volatility by cutting planned June bond sales about 21% from May, mainly in longer maturities. Finance ministry bond officials have also contacted dealers and asset managers directly and established a private chat group with market participants and researchers to monitor conditions.

Those measures can reduce near-term supply and improve communication, but they do not remove the forces behind higher yields. A large fiscal package would support demand at the same time the semiconductor boom is lifting activity and the won is increasing import costs. The Bank of Korea’s hawkish turn under Governor Shin Hyun Song leaves the market exposed to further repricing if core inflation remains firm.

Japanese institutional demand offered a countervailing flow for global bonds. Bank trust accounts, commonly used as proxies for pension funds, purchased a net ¥3.16 trillion of overseas bonds in May, the largest amount in data beginning in 2005. SMBC Nikko strategist Miki Den said a large share probably went to the U.S., where the 10-year Treasury yield had risen to 4.69% on May 19, its highest since January 2025.

The record is a backward-looking May flow rather than evidence that Japanese investors bought Monday’s Treasury selloff. It nevertheless shows that higher U.S. yields can attract large strategic demand even while Japanese government yields rise. The comparable Japanese yield remained about 200 basis points below the U.S. benchmark at its own mid-May peak, preserving a substantial yield differential before currency hedging and other costs.

Den expected purchases to slow in the near term because uncertainty over the Middle East and Fed policy remained elevated, then resume when those paths become clearer. That qualification is important for the coming U.S. auction cycle. Record demand in May establishes capacity and appetite, but geopolitical volatility and the prospect of Fed tightening can delay deployment precisely when Treasury is asking investors to absorb new coupon supply.

## Asian Credit Separates Refinancing Capacity From State Support

Indonesia’s market rout is beginning to intersect directly with new dollar funding. Sovereign wealth fund Danantara planned to begin the U.S. leg of its bond roadshow in Boston on June 9 before moving to New York the following day. In earlier Asian meetings, fund officials told some investors that part of the prospective proceeds could refinance a $1 billion loan raised earlier in 2026.

The offering comes as the rupiah reached a record low and Indonesian equities extended a decline driven by concern over President Prabowo Subianto’s interventionist economic agenda. The benchmark stock index fell more than 4% on Monday and had lost almost 40% in 2026. Indonesia’s 10-year government yield rose to its highest in more than a year, increasing pressure on finance and central-bank officials to supplement weekend assurances with concrete measures capable of attracting inflows.

Dollar sovereign bonds had been comparatively resilient. A basket of Indonesian government securities widened about 3 basis points during 2026 to 71 basis points as of Friday. High-grade Asian dollar bonds tightened 13 basis points over the same period to a record-low spread of 50 basis points. The contrast shows that Indonesia has underperformed a strong regional credit backdrop without yet experiencing the degree of disorder visible in its currency, local rates or equities.

Danantara’s legal relationship with the state will be central to the roadshow. Its offering memorandum said the government does not guarantee obligations on the notes. Proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes, including investments and refinancing outstanding borrowings. That distinction matters because the fund oversees nearly 900 state companies and is a prominent instrument of government economic policy, but its institutional role does not convert the proposed bonds into explicitly guaranteed sovereign debt.

The fund is also planning local-currency “Merah Putih” bonds carrying a 3% coupon, below prevailing market rates, for domestic and foreign investors. The simultaneous pursuit of dollar and subsidized local funding puts the emphasis on the terms investors receive and the exact source of repayment, particularly while policymakers are trying to stabilize the currency and restore confidence.

The Philippines faces a slower but sizeable corporate refinancing test. An inter-agency financial-stability report said large conglomerates have about 1.6 trillion pesos, or $26 billion, of debt maturing from 2027 through 2029. That represents nearly one-quarter of conglomerates’ total debt, while U.S. dollar obligations average 37.6% of their debt over the next five years.

Companies have so far met refinancing needs through bonds, bank funding and internal liquidity. The weak peso increases the local-currency burden of foreign obligations, however, and the Philippines imports almost all of its fuel from the Middle East. The combination of currency depreciation, higher energy costs and concentrated maturities raises both refinancing and foreign-exchange risk even without an immediate default event.

The report said banks remained sufficiently capitalized to absorb unexpected losses and able to continue lending. It also identified elevated property prices and growing unsecured consumer borrowing, mostly credit-card debt, as vulnerabilities. BSP Governor Eli Remolona said regulators would define when issues should be escalated and improve communication about the entities they supervise. The new information is therefore a quantified maturity and currency exposure within a system regulators still describe as stable.

Primary-market activity elsewhere showed investors continuing to finance large transactions. Tencent was preparing a dual-currency bond sale of about $3 billion that could price as early as Tuesday. Blackstone was seeking to turn more than $2 billion of stakes in private investment funds into bonds, potentially one of the largest transactions of its kind in recent years. Arcmont Asset Management and Ares were leading a €1.1 billion loan for Silver Lake-backed French software company Cegid. These deals indicate continued access to structured and leveraged financing, though they expose investors to different underlying cash flows from conventional senior corporate debt.

The broader macro risk remains the duration of the oil shock. A Peterson Institute for International Economics scenario examined oil near $120 a barrel for a full year alongside more expensive liquefied natural gas, refined fuels, agriculture and fertilizer. It estimated output relative to baseline would be at least 12% lower in the Middle East and North Africa, about 3% lower in India, Vietnam and Thailand, 2.8% lower in South Korea, 1.8% lower in China, 1.6% lower in Western Europe and 1.2% lower in the U.S.

Those are conditional model estimates, not forecasts, and oil finished Monday in the low-to-mid $90s. They nevertheless illustrate why the same shock can produce different credit outcomes. Energy importers face weaker growth, currency pressure and higher refinancing costs, while economies with stronger domestic demand may respond with tighter monetary policy. The U.S. is relatively insulated in the scenario, but its farming and transport sectors would still take larger hits than the aggregate economy.

## Forward Market Significance

The next Treasury test begins June 9 with $65 billion of 6-week bills and $50 billion of 52-week bills at 11:30 ET. The 6-week offering is $10 billion smaller than its predecessor, while the 52-week amount is unchanged. At 13:00 ET, Treasury will sell $58 billion of new 3-year notes, unchanged from the prior offering, for June 15 settlement. That auction will show whether higher yields are sufficient to draw demand into the policy-sensitive belly after two sessions of post-payroll losses.

U.S. CPI at 08:30 ET on June 10 is the decisive macro event. Headline inflation is expected to rise 0.5% on the month and 4.2% from a year earlier, following 0.6% and 3.8%. Core inflation is expected at 0.2% monthly and 2.9% annually after 0.4% and 2.8%. A result driven mainly by energy would be consistent with the decline in 10-year breakevens; broad core strength would validate the rise in real yields and strengthen the case for an eventual Fed increase.

Treasury will reopen $39 billion of 10-year notes at 13:00 ET after CPI. The securities carry a 4.375% coupon and settle June 15. The sequence links the week’s most important inflation release directly to a duration auction, making both the clearing level and bidder composition consequential after the 10-year real yield rose to 2.199%.

The ECB decides policy at 08:15 ET on June 11. A 25-basis-point increase would take the deposit rate to 2.25%, from 2%, but the more important question is whether the Governing Council presents the move as limited insurance or the start of repeated tightening. German industrial production on June 9, expected to rise 0.5% in April after a revised 0.1% decline, will indicate whether the order slump has already reached output.

U.S. producer prices and initial claims arrive at 08:30 ET on June 11. PPI is expected to rise 0.7% on the month, with the core measure up 0.5%, after revised increases of 1.4% and 1%. Claims will follow the prior week’s 225,000 reading and test whether household anxiety about job loss is beginning to appear in realized layoffs. Treasury then reopens $22 billion of 30-year bonds at 13:00 ET, completing the coupon cycle.

All three coupon issues settle June 15, producing $119 billion of gross settlement immediately before the June 16-17 FOMC meeting. That concentration will test dealer balance sheets and end-user demand after the long bond moved back above 5%. June 15 also brings U.S. industrial production, expected to increase 0.1% after a 0.9% gain, providing the final hard-activity update before the Fed decision.

The nearer Asian calendar starts with China’s May trade data on June 9 at 10:30 in Taipei. The trade surplus is expected at CNY625 billion after CNY585.6 billion, with export and import details determining whether external demand continues to support regional manufacturing. For Indonesia, Danantara’s Boston and New York meetings will test whether investors accept corporate-style risk from a state-owned fund without an explicit government guarantee. For Korea, the immediate question is whether reduced June bond issuance can slow a selloff rooted in stronger growth, core inflation and expectations for at least three Bank of Korea increases.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury selloff broadens as real yields and the long end absorb payroll strength and renewed oil risk
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended Friday’s payroll-driven selloff, but the move broadened from the policy-sensitive front end into a bear steepening. The 2-year yield rose 1.6 basis points to 4.164%, the 10-year added 3.3 basis points to 4.564% and the 30-year climbed 4 basis points to 5.037%. At 10 years, the real yield increased 3.7 basis points to 2.199% while breakeven inflation slipped 0.4 basis point to 2.365%, showing that investors demanded more inflation-adjusted compensation rather than extrapolating the energy shock into higher long-term inflation expectations.

The market remained under pressure from May’s stronger-than-expected payroll report and renewed Israel-Iran fighting, which lifted WTI 0.84% to $91.30 and Brent 1.25% to $94.25. A New York Fed survey tempered the hawkish case: one-year inflation expectations fell to 3.5%, longer-term readings held steady, and households reported greater concern about job loss, re-employment and debt payments. Those signals did not displace resilient realized employment or the immediate oil risk.

The cross-asset close was more constructive. Equities rebounded, semiconductor shares led gains, volatility fell and high-yield funds edged higher, arguing against a general flight from risk. The next test is whether CPI and the Treasury coupon cycle validate the rise in real yields while attracting sufficient demand at higher nominal rates.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields rose across the curve and the long end underperformed as strong employment and renewed Israel-Iran fighting sustained tightening and inflation concerns, while lower household inflation expectations and weaker confidence provided only a partial counterweight.
